title: No internet, expired sign-ins, and the startup screen that ends your session

steps.headline: How much review should these three fixes go through before they are built?
steps.today: New features normally go through questions, then pictures, then a written definition of done you sign, then a final acceptance round.
steps.problem: One of the three is a plain bug fix, but the other two add new messages to the app that you have not seen yet.
steps.proposal: Pick how many rounds you want to see before this is finished.

options.label: Pictures, then build
pros: You still see every new message before it is built.
Fewer rounds for a set of changes with clear direction.
cons: No signed checklist to hold the finished work against.

options.label: Full route
pros: A signed definition of done and a final yes/no on each part.
cons: Two more rounds for you to answer.

steps.page: The startup screen that ends your session
steps.intro: You press Yes on the folder question, type a message, press Enter, and the session closes.

steps.path: New conversation with skip permissions on
steps.headline: Cause found: on today's Claude Code, the app no longer recognises the folder question or the skip-permissions warning.
steps.changed: Tested against the Claude Code on this computer (2.1.271). Both screens dropped their numbered options, so the app's reader found no menu at all. The warning's first choice is "No, exit", already highlighted, so any Enter ends the session. The fix teaches the app both screens and pins them with a test built from the real ones.
steps.notice: Both screens appear as cards again, their buttons pick the choice you pressed, and a message you type can no longer answer one by accident.

steps.path: New conversation with skip permissions on
steps.headline: Should the skip-permissions warning be shown as a card, or answered automatically?
steps.today: When you start a conversation with skip permissions on, Claude Code asks you to confirm that choice on a screen of its own before it starts.
steps.problem: You already chose skip permissions when you started the conversation, so this is the second time you are asked.
steps.proposal: Either show the warning as a card with its two buttons, or accept it for you because you already turned the setting on.

options.label: Show a card
pros: You confirm a risky mode yourself, in Claude Code's own words.
Nothing is accepted on your behalf.
cons: One more tap when starting that kind of conversation.

options.label: Accept it for me
pros: The conversation starts with no extra step.
cons: The app accepts a safety warning you never read.
If Claude Code changes that screen, the app could answer the wrong thing.

steps.path: Any conversation that is still starting up
steps.headline: If you send a message while a startup question is still waiting, what should happen to it?
steps.today: Today the message goes straight to Claude Code, and if a startup question is on screen, your Enter answers it.
steps.problem: Even after the fix, a future Claude Code change could hide a new startup question from the app, and the same accident would come back.
steps.proposal: As a second safety net, a message sent before the conversation has finished starting never reaches Claude Code early. Pick what happens to it.

options.label: Hold and send
pros: Nothing to retype; it goes out as soon as the conversation is ready.
A bubble marked waiting shows it has not been sent yet.
cons: If the conversation never finishes starting, the message waits until you remove it.

options.label: Keep it in the box
pros: Simple: a short note says to answer the question above first.
cons: You have to press send again once it is ready.

steps.intro: Pressing sign-in or starting a conversation offline today ends in a timeout or a confusing error, never "no internet".

steps.path: Any sign-in button, and New conversation
steps.headline: The app says "no internet" only after its own check fails, never as a guess.
steps.changed: Before a sign-in or a new conversation on an online model, the app runs a quick check that it can reach the internet. It says "no internet" only when that check fails twice. Otherwise the real error is shown, as it is today.
steps.notice: "No internet" means exactly that, and a problem on the provider's side is never blamed on your connection.

steps.path: First launch screen, and Settings, Model Providers
steps.headline: When you press a sign-in button with no internet, should the app stop before opening the browser?
steps.today: Pressing Log in with Claude or Sign in with ChatGPT opens your browser straight away, whatever the connection.
steps.problem: Offline, the browser page never loads, and two minutes later the app says the sign-in timed out, which sounds like your fault.
steps.proposal: The app checks the connection first. With none, the browser stays closed and the message appears under the button you pressed, with Retry.

options.label: Stop and say so
pros: You learn the real reason in about a second.
Retry sits right where you pressed.
cons: On an unusual network that blocks the check but not sign-in, you would have to press Retry.

options.label: Open it anyway
options.summary: Open the browser as today, but show the no-internet note beside the waiting spinner.
pros: Never blocks a sign-in that might have worked.
cons: A browser tab opens onto an error page.

steps.path: New conversation, and the first message in it
steps.headline: Where should "no internet" appear when you start a conversation on an online model?
steps.today: The conversation opens, you type, and the message either hangs or shows a raw error such as "fetch failed".
steps.problem: Nothing tells you the conversation cannot work until you have already written and sent something.
steps.proposal: Pick where the message appears. Conversations on local models start normally, with no check at all.

options.label: Card in the chat
pros: Appears in the conversation, where you are looking.
Your message stays in the box, and Retry sends it once the connection is back.
cons: The conversation still opens, even though it cannot reply yet.

options.label: Before it opens
pros: You find out before choosing a folder or typing anything.
cons: Stops you opening old conversations or files that do not need the internet.

steps.headline: Should the same message also appear when the internet drops in the middle of a conversation?
steps.today: You did not ask about this, and today a dropped connection mid-reply shows a raw error or a stalled spinner.
steps.problem: Covering only sign-in and starting would leave the most common offline moment unexplained.
steps.proposal: Yes adds it now, using the same card and the same honest check. No keeps this work to sign-in and starting, and files the rest for later.

steps.intro: Claude, ChatGPT and OpenRouter sign-ins can end on their own. Today you find out when a message fails.

steps.headline: How often should the app check that your sign-ins still work?
steps.today: Claude is checked only when you open the model menu. ChatGPT renews itself and signs you out quietly if that fails. An OpenRouter key is never checked.
steps.problem: An expired sign-in stays hidden until a message fails, often with an error that does not say the sign-in is the reason.
steps.proposal: Every check is quiet and free. Pick when they run.

options.label: Regularly
options.summary: When the app opens, every 30 minutes after that, and straight away when a message fails.
pros: You usually hear before you need it, not after a failed message.
cons: A sign-in that ends between checks is still found on a failed message.

options.label: Only on failure
pros: Never checks unless something already went wrong.
cons: You always find out by losing a message first.

steps.headline: When a sign-in has run out, where should the app offer to sign you in again?
steps.today: Nowhere. The model menu greys out Claude models only once you open it, and ChatGPT's error names a settings page with no button.
steps.problem: You have to work out yourself that the sign-in is the problem, and then find where to fix it.
steps.proposal: Pick where the offer to sign in again appears.

options.label: Notice plus a dot
options.summary: A notice above the message box, only in conversations that use that provider, and a dot on Settings for the rest.
pros: Shown where it matters, and never in a conversation it does not affect.
Uses the notice spot and Settings dot the app already has.
cons: If you are not in an affected conversation, you only see the dot.

options.label: A pop-up
pros: Impossible to miss.
cons: Interrupts whatever you are doing, even in a conversation that is unaffected.

options.label: Settings dot only
pros: Quietest.
cons: Easy to miss until a message fails.

steps.headline: What should "Sign in again" do for Claude?
steps.today: Signing in to Claude inside the app exists only on the first launch screen. After that, the only way is typing /login in the terminal view.
steps.problem: Most people using the app will never find the terminal view, so an expired Claude sign-in is a dead end for them.

options.label: Browser, like first launch
pros: The same browser sign-in you did on day one, started from the button.
The app notices when it is done and clears the notice itself.
cons: Conversations that were already open may need reopening to use the new sign-in.

options.label: Open terminal, type /login
pros: Uses Claude Code's own sign-in, inside the conversation.
cons: Drops you into the terminal view with a list of sign-in types to pick from.

steps.headline: When OpenRouter rejects your key, what should the fix be?
steps.today: OpenRouter is connected by pasting a key. Its Test button only checks that OpenRouter's website is up, so a dead key still reads Connected.
steps.problem: A key you deleted or ran out of credit on looks fine until every message fails.
steps.proposal: The app will check the key itself. Pick what the fix offers when the key is refused.

options.label: Paste a new key
pros: Opens the connect window you already know, so it can ship with the rest.
cons: You still have to make the key on OpenRouter's website.

options.label: Browser sign-in
pros: One button, no key to copy.
cons: OpenRouter browser sign-in is not built yet, and building it would delay the rest.

steps.path: A message that failed because a sign-in ran out
steps.headline: After you sign in again, should the message that failed be sent again for you?
steps.today: In ChatGPT and OpenRouter conversations a Try again button resends it. In Claude Code conversations you type it again yourself.
steps.problem: Having to retype it after fixing the sign-in makes the fix feel like extra work.
steps.proposal: Yes shows a "Send it again" button on the notice once you are signed back in. No leaves resending to you.
